reference_approval: reviews/STATUS.md: S1–S15 and style tests APPROVED; newer Arc 3–5 sheets not used

attempts.prompt:
Korean webtoon panel, digitally inked and coloured by a professional webtoon studio. Crisp black ink with tapered strokes, heavier on the outer silhouette, the jaw, the hair mass and where forms overlap. Flat local colour with one hard-edged cool cel shadow per material. One named key light: its colour washes smoothly over the lit side. If the scene names a back light, it draws a thin crisp rim along the figure's silhouette. Everything else stays flat. Muted cool base palette of slate, navy and grey-blue, so the light source and the character's signature colour carry the saturation. Background simplified and lower in contrast than the characters. Small crisp highlights; glossy specular only on metal and wet surfaces.

Hand-made webtoon colouring: each garment has only a few large, opaque, clean-edged shadow shapes, placed in its real folds; no scattered translucent streaks, zigzag shards or crumpled-foil folds. Worn cloth shows a few small frayed notches and loose threads, never sawtooth edges along every edge. Plain shoes and clothes with no logos, stripes or brand marks. Every strap, buckle, pocket and seam is attached and has a purpose; no stray stitch marks. Matte skin, hair and stone; no 3D, low-poly or plastic look.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one production PROP MODEL SHEET, landscape 1536 x 1024 PNG, full native resolution.
Recipe: insert/reference-sheet, clean isolated object views on perfectly flat solid light grey #E9E9EC. Soft neutral key light from upper left; very short contact shadows only. No scene, vignette, gradient backdrop, borders, dividing lines, label boxes, people, hands or scale silhouettes. Use generous clear separation between the objects. Eight distinct main prop types plus their hardware detail views. Different detail vignettes may be magnified independently; no scale ruler. Every item fully inside the canvas.
Reference 1 is the approved knight detail sheet: use ONLY its industrial matte-black chain material and its simple recessed DIAMOND/RHOMBUS stamp, seen on the chain link at bottom centre. No knight, helm, face hole, towers, blade or armour on this new sheet.
Reference 2 is the approved acting image: linework and restrained clean cel colouring only. Copy no face, hair, red lighting, pencil or character.

LAYOUT AND CONTENT:
UPPER THIRD: the long anchor assembly occupies the upper-left two thirds. Show a complete TWO-METRE black-steel industrial HARPOON ANCHOR, a straight long steel shank with pointed penetrator nose and two sturdy backward-facing forged barbs, not a boat's curved stock anchor. The tail eye is joined by ONE BIG U-shaped steel shackle and its clearly visible removable transverse pin to a short length of very heavy arm-thick factory-steel oval chain. Uniform links alternate at right angles and really pass through one another. The barbed head, shank, eye, shackle and chain must be a mechanically coherent single assembly, no disconnected end or useless ring. Matte dark iron with a few crisp steel edges and sparse worn scratches, never chrome.
At upper-right give TWO separate magnified hardware detail views: one OPEN U-shaped heavy steel shackle with two aligned pierced lugs and its single removable cross-pin withdrawn beside it, the pin's axis exactly aligned with both lug holes, readable as the part a scout can knock out; beside/below it one enlarged closed oval chain LINK with a flattened stamped pad carrying a small recessed diamond outline identical to reference 1. This is a geometric stamp, never a letter. These are explicitly enlarged details of the assembly, not extra weapon types.

MIDDLE BAND, three clean spacious vignettes:
Left: the Deep Lantern's CORE, head-sized (about 25 cm tall), shaped like a real small lantern but made from organic pale coral. An open rounded cage of a few curved branching bone-white coral ribs around a slowly pulsing WHITE-VIOLET light, white centre and faint lilac margins. Hollow gaps clearly visible between the ribs. A small pale coral cap and base make a portable lantern silhouette. No metallic gothic ornament, no chain, no candle, no huge leviathan lantern or creature.
Centre: Pim's black over-ear GAMING HEADSET, unbranded, slightly oversized, two thick black padded earcups, a plastic headband with ONE visible hairline crack near its crown. Leave an open gap inside the arch where the antennae would pass; do not draw antennae. On the outside earcup show a DEAD light ring as an unlit dark-grey ring. Absolutely no LEDs or coloured illumination on the headset. A small sensible boom microphone attached to one earcup is fine.
Right: Sora's NEW slim SILVER-CASED CORE COMPASS, a small round shallow silver case with clear glass face, a central pivot, and a SINGLE needle made from a narrow smoky violet shard of core. The needle glows faintly violet, not cyan. Fine silver bracelet chain attached to an actual eyelet on the case, laid as a wrist-sized loop, with a functional clasp. Unlettered dial: no N E S W, no numerals, no runes. It is silver rather than brass; not a wristwatch.

LOWER THIRD, four separated vignettes:
Left: Geum's BIG LONG-HANDLED STEEL LADLE close up, diagonally placed so its complete continuous long plain shaft and deep round bowl are visible. Practical kitchen utensil, no sword, hammer or magical staff. Bowl interior holds concentrated WHITE force, white glowing inside with only a tight thin white edge just outside the lip. The bowl and metal rim remain legible; no whole-sheet bloom, no gold/cyan/violet on the ladle.
Left-centre small: a WOODEN CHOPSTICK FINGER SPLINT, one short straight light-tan wooden chopstick with two neat white medical tape loops wrapped around it, shaped to support a right index finger. Display the prepared splint alone, no floating skin, disembodied finger, blood or hand.
Right-centre: the market's BATTERED RED MEGAPHONE, a practical red conical plastic horn, dark speaker cone recessed in the mouth, attached pistol handle and small off-white rear battery body, a few scuffed paint chips. Three-quarter view makes the hollow horn opening, rear body, handle and trigger coherent. No label or writing.
Right: a CHEAP ROUND PLASTIC WALL CLOCK, pale off-white casing, clear flat face, black hour and minute hands and a thin second hand pointing to different angles, twelve plain short radial index strokes. NO DIGITS, no numerals, words or brand name. Ordinary cheap household clock, not an alarm clock or compass.

All specified objects present, clearly readable with crisp outlines and large opaque cel shadows. Hardware, microphone and wrist-chain attachments must make mechanical sense. Background remains flat and empty around them; effects stay confined to their actual light sources.


No text, letters, numbers, speech bubbles, captions, sound-effect lettering, interface windows or readable signs. Emblems without letters are fine; no brand logos or wordmarks. Not a 3D render, not a photograph, no photographic background. No airbrushed skin, no plastic gloss on skin or hair, no haze or bloom over the whole image, no depth-of-field blur, no lens flare unless a real camera flash is in the scene. No watermark or signature. Correct hands with five fingers. No chibi proportions unless the brief says chibi. No compressed or stubby bodies, no shortened legs or torsos, no oversized heads; no people out of scale with the doors, vehicles and buildings around them; no figures floating off the floor or breaking the scene's perspective.
reasons: Ladle force has a violet tint rather than neutral white.
Detached shackle pin axis not aligned with lug bores; assembled pin unclear.
Clock has doubled index strokes; ladle exterior has faceted shading.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit reference image 1, the props sheet, into the final production model sheet. Preserve the same landscape 1536 x 1024 canvas, entire layout, object silhouettes, all eight prop types and both magnified hardware views. Preserve the light-grey background, diamond stamps, coral core's white-violet glow, headset with its cracked headband and UNLIT earcup ring, slim silver compass and fine bracelet chain, wooden chopstick with white tape, battered red megaphone and unlettered clock.
TARGETED CORRECTION to force/material separation and hardware:
1. Geum's ladle bowl at lower left must hold PURE NEUTRAL WHITE light, no lavender, violet, blue, cyan or gold tint anywhere inside the bowl or rim. White centre with a neutral silver-grey boundary. Keep the metal rim and bowl depth obvious. A tight white glow confined inside its bowl. Make the ladle's exterior metal one flat dark steel base and ONE clean dark curved cel shadow, with two simple narrow white edge highlights. Remove triangular low-poly bevel facets from its bowl and remove busy reflected shards; it is a hand-inked utensil.
2. The magnified U-shackle at upper right must have exactly two round lugs with visible aligned circular cross-holes, at exactly the same height and seen on one common axis. Position the ONE detached steel cross-pin immediately to the right with its long axis exactly passing through the centres of both lug holes: a simple exploded engineering view, not perspective axes that miss each other. No extra eye holes in the pin. It has a flat round head and a plain cylindrical shaft, easily driven out.
3. On the long harpoon's tail connector, explicitly show the removable shackle's transverse pin seated across its two ears, joining its solid tail eye to the first chain link. This connector must read as pinned, not welded or a chain magically threaded through a solid rod.
4. Clean the clock's radial index marks to twelve evenly spaced single short strokes, with NO double strokes, no digits, no letters. Preserve its two heavy hands and one thin second hand.
Reduce surface scratch clutter and polygon facets throughout to a few intentional clean marks. All edges sharp and inked, all colour shapes large and opaque; no CG shine or 3D shading. Keep every object wholly in frame with clear space between objects. No people, body parts, labels, arrows or text.
Reference image 2 supplies ONLY the existing small diamond stamp shape and clean chain material; do not add its armour or sword. Reference image 3 supplies ONLY hand-inked cel colouring technique; no character or red scene light.

No text, letters, numbers, speech bubbles, captions, sound-effect lettering, interface windows or readable signs. Emblems without letters are fine; no brand logos or wordmarks. - Its straight removable cylindrical CROSS-PIN passes through the two ears AND through the anchor tail eye, locking them together. In this side view the pin axis comes toward the viewer; show its unmistakable LARGE ROUND FLAT PIN HEAD on the near ear, at the centre of the connection, with a crisp narrow circular rim. The other end seats behind the far ear.
- The shackle's rounded bow reaches rightward and actually passes through the first oval chain link. The bow, cross-pin, tail eye and chain form one attached plausible mechanism. Leave clear negative space in the bow so this is readable.
- The round cross-pin head is the part Nib knocks out to free the boss; it must be easy to see, separate from the shaft. No long sleeve or collar enclosing the shaft in place of a pin.
Keep the scale, existing connector location and occupied footprint. Matte black forged steel, clean outlines, a few large opaque grey cel shapes, only narrow metallic highlights. Do not redraw the anchor head or any other props.
Reference 2 is material/stamp continuity only, no armour or sword.

review: All P2 props present; no text, labels, numbers, people or silhouettes.
Anchor attachment shows a round removable cross-pin head; separate shackle, pin and diamond-stamped link shown.
Ladle force neutral white; core white-violet; headset ring unlit; compass silver.
Viewed full native image, 200px-wide thumbnail in memory, and a representative hardware detail at 200% zoom.
